From The Federalist Papers:

If standing armies are dangerous to liberty, an efficacious power over the militia, in the body to whose care the protection of the State is committed, ought, as far as possible, to take away the inducement and the pretext to such unfriendly institutions. (emphasis mine)

Back when the Articles of Confederation were failing miserably, arguments against a stronger central government included opposition to a standing army. The reasoning was that said army could be used by said central government to, essentially, enact tyranny. It was felt, therefore, that a better system for national defense would be militia, ordinary citizens who would be called to duty when the need arose. Therefore, the reference to "a well-regulated militia" is, in fact, a reference to citizens called upon to defend their country.

In other words, the 2nd Amendment does NOT grant the right for every citizen to own any and all weapons they fucking feel like. It says that the people must be allowed to keep and bear arms in order to defend the country in lieu of a standing army. Since we now have a standing army, the militia is no longer needed. If anything, the existence of a standing army nullifies the right of the general populace to keep and bear arms. The general populace is not called upon to maintain the "security of a free State" anymore, so the justification for unrestricted weapon possession no longer applies.

TL;DR -- Gun ownership was originally intended for national defense, not personal defense. Your argument against gun control legislation is invalid.
